claims.claim: The corpus contains 456 unique works spanning 2018–2023, acquired exhaustively and exactly deduplicated.
Metadata coverage is complete for seven core fields, with 85.09% abstract, 97.37% DOI, 96.05% publisher, and 99.56% language coverage.
Annual output rose from 1 in 2018 to 190 in 2023 and endpoint CAGR was 185.6%.
Briefings in Bioinformatics, Thin Nguyen, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences lead source, author, and institution productivity.
Bradford Zone 1 contains 5 sources and 148 documents, demonstrating source concentration.
Mean citations are 59.82, median 24.00, 22 works are uncited, and the maximum is 1,210.
GraphDTA is the most-cited included work and Attentive FP is second.
Six social, conceptual, and intellectual networks were constructed with association-strength normalization and Louvain clustering.
The reported node, edge, and cluster structures for the six displayed networks are correct.
The keyword map has a computational core and the coupling map separates several document communities.
Institutional collaboration is largely nationally bounded and especially concentrated within China.
The cocitation base is anchored by seminal GNN and molecular-featurization papers.
The field has a computational-methods core and biomedical-application periphery and is diversifying into geometry-enhanced, self-supervised, and interpretable architectures.
The direct-citation network is sparse because of the narrow time window and citations extending outside the corpus.
The corpus contains 456 unique works spanning 2018–2023, acquired by exhausted cursor pagination and exact deduplication.
The stated metadata field coverage percentages are correct.
Annual output peaked at 190 in 2023 and endpoint CAGR was 185.60%.
Briefings in Bioinformatics, Thin Nguyen, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences are the leading source, author, and institution.
The source-supplied document type is article for all 456 works, but that label cannot establish absence of review content.
Bradford Zone 1 has 5 sources and 148 documents and Zone 3 has 120 sources and 151 documents.
Bradford-zone document counts were rounded to the nearest 50.
Mean citations are 59.82, median 24.00, 22 works are uncited, and the maximum is 1,210.
GraphDTA and Attentive FP are the top two cited works with 1,210 and 1,056 citations.
Keyword, coauthorship, institution, coupling, cocitation, and direct-citation network sizes and cluster counts are as reported.
All three leading keywords increased every year.
The direct-citation network's sparsity is caused by the short citation window and thresholding.
The field is in a hot-topic or nascent phase and is method-driven.
The report explicitly cautions about source dependence, citation windows, metadata limits, network parameters, abstract-only inference, and productivity-quality distinctions.

rationale: B covers nearly all performance and mapping outputs while being materially more disciplined about metadata classification, parameter sensitivity, abstract-only inference, and productivity versus quality. A is broader and polished but repeatedly turns layouts and clusters into unsupported geographic, intellectual, and future-trend conclusions.

claims.claim: The corpus contains 259 unique publications from 2015–2022, retrieved exhaustively and exactly deduplicated.
The stated metadata completeness values are correct.
Output rose from 2 in 2015 to 72 in 2022 and endpoint CAGR was 66.85%.
The growth series has emergence, acceleration, and consolidation phases.
All records are source-labelled articles, so the field is dominated by primary research rather than reviews.
Mean citations are 72.09, median 32.00, maximum 1,436, and 35 works are uncited.
The leading cited works and their citation counts concern Pseudomonas, RNA delivery, hybrid EV–liposome CRISPR delivery, EV drug delivery, circular RNA, and nanoparticle CRISPR delivery.
Those top-cited works prove that EV–CRISPR therapeutic delivery dominates the impact landscape.
Xiaohui Chen leads author output; Harvard, Peking, and Sun Yat-sen tie for institutional leadership; International Journal of Molecular Sciences leads sources.
The reported coauthorship and institution-network node, edge, cluster, degree, and layout statistics are correct.
Bradford zoning consists of 23, 66, and 85 sources contributing 85, 87, and 85 documents.
The keyword counts, five-cluster network, and displayed map statistics are correct.
The overlay demonstrates that newer work concentrates on applied therapeutic themes.
The coupling and cocitation network sizes, clusters, top nodes, and layout statistics are correct.
The field is rapidly maturing toward clinical relevance, and preclinical validation and clinical translation will define its next phase.
The report acknowledges source, citation-window, parameterization, abstract-only, keyword, and final-year limitations.
The corpus contains 259 unique works spanning 2015–2022, acquired exhaustively and exactly deduplicated.
The stated metadata completeness percentages are correct.
Output peaked at 72 in 2022 and endpoint CAGR was 66.85%, with a four-paper decline in 2021.
International Journal of Molecular Sciences, Xiaohui Chen, and Harvard University lead source, author, and institution productivity.
Harvard, Peking, and Sun Yat-sen Universities tie at seven publications.
Bradford Zone 1 comprises 23 sources and 85 documents.
Mean citations are 72.09, median 32.00, maximum 1,436, and 35 works are uncited.
The most-cited work is a 2022 Pseudomonas aeruginosa review with 1,436 citations and appears tangential to the EV–CRISPR intersection.
The five mapped networks use the reported association-strength, Louvain, layout, threshold, and edge-reduction procedures.
The keyword, coupling, coauthorship, institution, and cocitation maps have the reported displayed sizes and cluster counts.
The evidence establishes a trans-Pacific institutional axis.
Collaboration is strongly intra-institutional and intra-national with emerging cross-cluster links.
The thematic structure is dominated by EV-mediated CRISPR delivery and translational application is the primary driver.
The report clearly states source, citation-window, metadata, full-text, network, and productivity limitations.

rationale: B provides similarly broad quantitative and network coverage with substantially better caution, including flagging the top-cited outlier and refusing to equate network centrality with substantive importance. A is richer in detail but repeatedly promotes descriptive clusters, dates, and abstracts into unsupported maturation, dominance, national-structure, and clinical-trajectory claims.
